profiles.description: Chief executive of this multi-line carrier, accountable to the board for enterprise strategy and performance across the life, annuity, disability/absence, retirement services, and P&C segments. Per the packet, the role prepares and presents the board reporting pack, sponsors major transformation initiatives, and approves executive hires and compensation. It also represents the company externally with investors, regulators, and rating agencies, consistent with the widened transformation and stakeholder remit sources describe for modern insurance CEOs. The role has no direct value-stream or task wiring in the operating model, reflecting its position above the seventeen value streams rather than within any one of them.

sources.title: What Makes a Great Insurance CEO? Key Skills for 2025 and Beyond — Hanover Search
Chief executive officer — Wikipedia

profiles.notes: Priors (roleFamily Executive, roleLevel Executive) confirmed by research. Empty valueStreams/tasks/deliverables is expected for the apex role, not a data gap.

profiles.description: Senior finance executive leading the Finance & Investments division, with Lead accountability for the Finance Investments and Finance, Treasury & Capital Management value streams. The role owns issuance of the carrier's financial statements — reviewing and approving them for release and obtaining controller sign-off on the GAAP consolidation — and participates in solvency filings to regulators, capital allocation reconciliation, and investor relations outputs such as the quarterly financial supplement and earnings release tables. Consistent with insurance-CFO sources, the role owns financial strategy, planning, controls, and external reporting, and coordinates with actuarial, investments, and risk on capital and liquidity decisions. It also participates in supplier quarterly business reviews on the operations side of the finance function.

sources.title: Role of CFO in Insurance Companies — Profitjets
What is a Chief Financial Officer — Umbrex Guide to Corporate Titles

profiles.notes: Participant on 'Submit Solvency Filings To Regulators And Obtain Officer Certification' is defensible (statutory reporting team owns execution; CFO certifies), so not flagged.

profiles.description: Top people executive of the carrier, setting people strategy, workforce planning, and culture priorities and ensuring talent, rewards, and employee relations support business goals. Per the packet, the role participates in defining the pay philosophy and target competitive positioning, benchmarking executive pay against the proxy peer group, and compiling executive compensation data for committee review — matching sources that place CHROs at the center of executive compensation and board compensation-committee work. It sponsors performance, compensation, and organizational design decisions and coordinates leadership development and change communications. The role supports the Human Resources Talent and Enterprise Strategy & Portfolio Management value streams.

sources.title: Chief human resources officer — Wikipedia
Five Key Responsibilities of Chief Human Resources Officers — Indeed

profiles.notes: Packet lists the CHRO as only Support (not Lead) on the Human Resources Talent value stream, which is unusual for the function's top executive — likely a value-stream relation gap rather than a role-definition issue (value-stream relations are outside the NodeRole/RoleDeliverable flag scope). All three sample tasks are Participant with zero Owner tasks and no deliverables, thin wiring for a C-suite role.

profiles.description: Enterprise security executive leading the Cybersecurity Iam and Cybersecurity, Identity & Resilience value streams, owning cybersecurity strategy, the policy framework, and security risk oversight. Per the packet, the role owns publishing security policies and confirming employee attestation, preparing the security risk report for the governance committee, approving material application-security risk acceptances, and obtaining executive attestation for the cyber resilience regulatory filing — duties that align with the NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law's requirement for a designated leader of the insurer's information security program with board-level reporting. It also participates in threat modeling for high-risk applications and in scoping and rating cyber risk assessments across business domains. The packet additionally assigns ownership of operational IAM tasks such as entitlement fulfillment and SSO certificate rotation, which sit below the strategic level sources describe for the role.

sources.title: The Evolving Role of the CISO in the Insurance Industry — Eliot Partnership
Insurance Topics: Cybersecurity — NAIC

classificationFlags.item: Fulfill Approved Entitlement Grant To Target System
classificationFlags.rationale: Eliot Partnership describes the CISO as an enterprise risk and governance executive aligned with the C-suite and board, not the hands-on fulfiller of individual access grants — an IAM analyst/engineer should own this task.

classificationFlags.item: Rotate Sso Signing And Encryption Certificates
classificationFlags.rationale: Per Eliot Partnership the CISO role has moved from technical execution to strategic oversight; certificate rotation is an identity/security engineering operational task the CISO governs rather than performs.

profiles.notes: roleFamily is a vocab stretch: the controlled vocabulary has no Security/Technology-Risk family, so Engineering (matching the Cybersecurity & IAM technology division) was chosen; Risk & Compliance was the runner-up given the role's heavy governance content.

profiles.description: Senior technology executive in the Technology & Engineering division, leading the Technology Engineering and Technology Strategy, Architecture & Delivery value streams and setting the enterprise technology strategy, operating model, and delivery priorities. Per the packet, the role owns enterprise architecture governance — maintaining EA principles and reference models and assessing project designs for compliance with architecture standards — plus recertifying the standard change library against failure data. This matches sources describing the insurance CIO as the gatekeeper for system reliability, integration quality, ROI on technology investment, and governance across the technology stack, while also acting as a digital transformation agent. The role coordinates with architecture, engineering, security, data, finance, and business leadership and approves technology policy changes, exceptions, and investment requests.

sources.title: Carrier Stories — Journey of a Chief Information Officer — IVANS
The digital disruption in insurance: How the role of a CIO has changed — EasySend

profiles.notes: The CIO and CTO share the same org home (Technology & Engineering / Executive Leadership) and lead the same value streams; in this org the CIO owns enterprise architecture governance while the CTO owns solution architecture assurance — a workable but slightly inverted split versus the common CTO/Enterprise-Architect pairing. Ownership of 'Maintain The Enterprise Architecture Principles And Reference Models' would often sit with a Chief/Enterprise Architect, but sources support the CIO as governance gatekeeper, so not flagged.

profiles.description: Head of the Investments department within Finance & Investments, leading the Finance Investments and Investment & Asset Management value streams for the carrier's general account. Per the packet, the role owns routing the Investment Policy Statement for investment committee approval and sign-off, and sets investment strategy aligned to liabilities, liquidity, and risk appetite. Consistent with sources on insurance CIOs, it monitors liquidity, duration, credit, and concentration exposures, reviews market conditions, asset allocation, and manager performance, and coordinates with finance, actuarial, and risk on investment decisions — the asset-liability management orientation that distinguishes an insurer's investment chief. It supports the Finance, Treasury & Capital Management and Enterprise Strategy & Portfolio Management streams.

sources.title: Chief investment officer — Wikipedia
Chief Investment Officer — Accounting.com

profiles.notes: Only one wired task/deliverable (Investment Policy & Mandate Setting) — thin but accurate; the single Owner link matches the role's signature accountability per both sources.

profiles.description: Top marketing executive in the Sales, Distribution & Marketing division, leading the Sales Distribution Marketing and Marketing, Growth & Customer Insights value streams. Per the packet, the role owns marketing budget management and planning — tracking campaign spend against budget and flagging overruns — and participates in defining brand positioning and value proposition by customer segment. It sets enterprise marketing strategy, brand direction, and demand generation priorities, oversees campaign investment, channel mix, and marketing performance, and approves brand standards, major campaigns, and marketing investment priorities. Sources confirm this budget/ROI accountability, brand-positioning ownership, and campaign approval authority as core CMO duties, coordinated with product, distribution, customer service, and digital teams.

sources.title: Chief Marketing Officer Job Description and Salary — LHH
Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) Job Description — Indeed

profiles.notes: Owner on the spend-tracking task is analyst-level work in isolation, but LHH explicitly assigns CMOs direct accountability for 'marketing budgets, forecasts, and ROI analysis', so the deliverable-level ownership stands.

profiles.description: Right hand to the CEO in the Office of the CEO, translating CEO priorities into a tracked executive agenda with owners, milestones, and decision dates. Per the packet, the role runs the weekly executive leadership meeting cadence (capturing decisions, actions, and escalations), coordinates board and executive committee material preparation with the Corporate Secretary, and brokers cross-divisional escalations between P&C and Life & Retirement leaders before they reach the CEO. It also leads confidential special projects spanning strategy, regulatory response, and transformation, and tracks enterprise OKRs and initiative health from performance-governance packs. Sources describe exactly this profile — a trusted advisor who drives planning cadence, board preparation, and cross-functional strategic initiatives on the executive's behalf.

sources.title: Chief of Staff Job Description — Indeed

profiles.notes: Prior said roleLevel 'Management'; research pushes higher — Indeed calls it 'an executive position' and The Alexander Group places it on C-suite rosters, but it carries no line P&L or functional authority, so Senior Leadership (not Executive) is the best fit of the output vocab. Prior disagreement recorded; family prior 'Executive Office' confirmed.

profiles.description: Enterprise operations executive in the Operations & Customer Service division, leading the Corporate Functions Operations value stream. Per the packet, the role owns operations performance monitoring and reporting — approving published performance metrics for distribution — and participates in incident response and crisis management governance, defining crisis roles, escalation thresholds, and decision authority and convening the incident bridge during major disruptions. It sets the operating model, service performance, and transformation priorities, ensures core operations scale efficiently and comply with controls, and coordinates operations priorities across underwriting, claims, finance, and technology. Sources confirm the insurance COO as the CEO-accountable executive for daily operations, service performance, process improvement, and operational compliance, while noting the role's scope varies with the CEO relationship.

sources.title: Insurance – Chief Operating Officer (COO) — Stonewood Group
What It Takes to Be a P/C Insurer COO: Executive Recruiter Views — Carrier Management

profiles.notes: Carrier Management notes COO scope is highly contextual ('Mr. Internal' vs de facto president); this org's packet defines it as the internal operations-performance and resilience owner, which is one of the two standard archetypes.

profiles.description: Enterprise insurance product executive in Product, Delivery & PMO, leading the Product Delivery, Product & Proposition Management, and Sales Distribution Marketing value streams. Per the packet, the role owns go-live readiness — conducting the go/no-go review and recording the launch decision with conditions — and participates in securing investment committee approval and funding for product business cases. It sets product strategy, portfolio priorities, and target customer outcomes, aligns product governance and lifecycle controls across lines of business, and approves product changes, launch readiness decisions, and portfolio investment priorities. Sources confirm the CPO as owner of the product lifecycle from ideation through launch and retirement, coordinating roadmaps with underwriting, actuarial, distribution, marketing, operations, and technology.

Insurance Product Lifecycle Explained — IB Applications

classificationFlags.item: File State Appointment With The Department Of Insurance Via Nipr
classificationFlags.rationale: Product School scopes the CPO to product strategy, lifecycle, and launch decisions; filing producer appointments via NIPR is a producer-licensing/distribution-operations task that should be owned by a licensing or producer governance role.

profiles.notes: roleFamily 'Product & Distribution' chosen over plain 'Product' because the packet wires the role as Lead of Sales Distribution Marketing and Support of Distribution & Channel Management in addition to the product streams.

profiles.description: Second-line executive leading the Risk Compliance Audit and Risk, Compliance & Regulatory Management value streams, owning the enterprise risk framework, risk appetite, and risk reporting. Per the packet, the role owns submitting the risk appetite framework for governance approval, approving and distributing the risk committee pack, obtaining governance sign-off on the control framework baseline and the assurance plan, and securing executive and board sign-off on the operational resilience regulatory submission — matching the regulatory pattern in which enterprise risk and ORSA-style filings must be signed by the CRO or the executive responsible for ERM oversight. It also participates in compliance governance reporting, three-lines assurance coordination and combined assurance reporting, and business impact analysis endorsement. The role chairs risk governance reviews and challenges business risk decisions across underwriting, finance, operations, and technology.

sources.title: Enterprise Risk Report and ORSA Summary Report — NY Department of Financial Services
Enterprise Risk Management Requirements of ORSA — LogicGate

profiles.notes: Packet also makes the CRO co-Lead of Corporate Functions Operations (shared with the COO), which is broader than the classic second-line remit but consistent with this org's resilience/assurance wiring; not a flaggable NodeRole conflict.

profiles.description: Head of Corporate Strategy & Development in the Executive Office, leading the annual enterprise strategy refresh across the P&C and Life & Retirement segments with the executive team. Per the packet, the role defines the target-state portfolio mix, growth bets, and divestment candidates for board approval, sponsors the strategic planning calendar that feeds funding and capital-allocation decisions with the CFO, and sets measurable strategic objectives cascaded into the enterprise OKR framework. It commissions quarterly market, competitor, and regulatory scans through Marketing's market-intelligence process and arbitrates cross-divisional strategy conflicts, presenting trade-offs to the CEO and board. Sources confirm this formulation-plus-portfolio remit — strategy development, portfolio optimization, growth/divestment decisions, and cascading objectives — as the core of the C-level CSO role.

sources.title: What Is a Chief Strategy Officer (CSO)? — TechTarget
Chief Strategy Officer (CSO) Job Description — Indeed

profiles.notes: Priors (roleFamily Executive Office, roleLevel Executive) confirmed. No value-stream/task wiring in the packet; responsibilities are the grounding — the strategy function appears to operate through the Enterprise Strategy & Portfolio Management stream owned via other roles.

profiles.description: Engineering-side technology executive in Technology & Engineering, leading the Technology Engineering and Technology Strategy, Architecture & Delivery value streams alongside the CIO. Per the packet, the role owns publishing and socializing the technology roadmap with delivery and business stakeholders, validating solution alignment to the enterprise reference architecture, validating designs against enterprise standards and guardrails, and reporting change risk posture and KRI breaches to governance. It participates in technology vendor/product evaluation and grants design authority approval at implementation gates. This matches sources describing the CTO as the setter of technology direction who establishes architecture guardrails, principles, and standards, oversees engineering teams and platform modernization, and translates technology capability into business outcomes.

sources.title: The Chief Technology Officer Role: Skills, Responsibilities, and Career Path — Splunk
Mercury Insurance Hires Chief Technology Officer to Drive Digital Strategy — PR Newswire

profiles.notes: CTO and CIO share org home and lead the same streams; the packet divides them coherently (CTO = roadmap, solution/design assurance, change risk; CIO = EA governance, standard change library). Owner-heavy design-assurance tasks would typically delegate to a design authority/chief architect day-to-day, but ownership at the accountable-executive level is consistent with Splunk's description, so not flagged.

profiles.description: Most senior underwriting executive, leading the Underwriting, Submission-to-Bind / Underwriting, and Business Operations value streams and setting underwriting strategy, risk appetite, and delegated authority for the carrier. Per the packet, the role owns appetite and guideline management (sign-off on revised appetite and guidelines, updating guidelines from governance decisions), authority sign-off decisions with conditions at senior referral, appetite exception logging, approval of revised zonal catastrophe capacity allocation, and approval and execution of renewed binding authority agreements following coverholder audits. Sources confirm these as the signature CUO accountabilities: owning appetite statements, authorities, and referral protocols, governing delegated underwriting authority with audits and renewals, and managing catastrophe accumulation within enterprise risk appetite. The role balances growth, portfolio quality, and underwriting profitability, coordinating with actuarial, claims, and reinsurance on market actions.

sources.title: Chief Underwriting Officer — JD Preferred (job posting)
What is a Delegated Authority? — Genasys Glossary

classificationFlags.item: Re Rate The Renewal And Apply Rate And Exposure Changes
classificationFlags.rationale: The JD Preferred CUO profile scopes the role to strategy, guidelines, authorities, and reviewing escalated complex submissions — re-rating an individual renewal is desk-underwriter execution work, not a CUO-owned task.

profiles.notes: Packet's CUO footprint includes P&C-specific machinery (coverholders, binding authority, catastrophe accumulation) confirming the carrier's P&C signals alongside its life/retirement lines.

profiles.description: Front-line claims professional in the Claims Handling department who investigates, evaluates, and resolves claims across the Claims Intake-to-Settlement value stream. Per the packet, the role owns the core of the claim file: capturing incident detail and supporting evidence, matching the loss notice to the in-force policy and verifying coverage, premium status, and scheduled property, calculating limits, sublimits, deductibles, and exhaustion, assigning initial loss and expense reserves at intake, issuing reservation-of-rights letters, and developing the investigation plan including required evidence and information sources. This matches O*NET and related occupational profiles, which define the occupation by investigating claims, examining forms and records to determine coverage, adjusting reserves, interviewing claimants and witnesses, and negotiating settlements. The role coordinates experts, vendors, counsel, and repair partners and manages claim files within policy terms and delegated authority.
